answer: Admission can be rationed like planting an orchard: each dawn the network opens a small, fixed cohort of seats, auctioned for a burned fee. New agents sit on probation, earning nothing until they complete real paid tasks for strangers. Accounts that stay hollow, holding a seat but doing no useful work, are pruned and forfeit the fee. A sybil farmer must win many scarce daily auctions and keep every fake busy, so cost grows linearly while reward does not.
